title: Insilico Medicine nominates AI-designed ISM1354 GIPR antagonist for obesity
key_facts: Insilico Medicine (HKEX: 3696) announced the nomination of ISM1354, an AI-designed small-molecule preclinical candidate that blocks the GIPR receptor, for obesity and related disorders such as type 2 diabetes.

Insilico says ISM1354 keeps robust weight-loss efficacy while improving on the safety and pharmacokinetic profile of its earlier GIPR antagonist ISM0676, which showed up to 31.3% weight loss with semaglutide in humanized mouse models (announced in January 2026).
Insilico reports oral bioavailability of 75-104% across mice, rats, dogs and monkeys, and at least 18-fold greater plasma exposure than a clinical-stage benchmark compound at the same dose.
In a non-GLP monkey toxicology assessment, Insilico says ISM1354 was generally well tolerated with an estimated ~45-fold margin of safety, supporting a move into GLP toxicology studies.
The release notes that several GIPR candidates from others have stumbled in clinical trials because of toxicity and tolerability issues.
Insilico says it has nominated 10 preclinical candidates in the first 9 months of 2026 and 34 since 2021.
The company's release is dated 30 Sep 2026; Drug Target Review covered it on 2 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: In a non-GLP monkey toxicology assessment, ISM1354 was generally well tolerated and exhibited a favorable safety profile, with no significant toxicity findings observed.

Preclinical evaluation showed that ISM1354 possesses outstanding and highly consistent pharmacokinetic characteristics across multiple species, including mice, rats, dogs, and monkeys, achieving oral bioavailability of 75-104%.
However, several GIPR candidates have recently stumbled in clinical trials due to toxicity and tolerability issues.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI-designed obesity drug candidate has passed early animal safety checks according to its maker, but it has not been tested in people.
event_date: 30 Sep 2026 (Insilico announcement); Drug Target Review published 2 Oct 2026.
